title: Classify integer-shift cubic repairs at odd S and certify twenty general-frame arities (no κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This PR adds the research package `research/cubic-odd-s-shift-floor`: scoped proofs, a complete finite classification and exact certificates. **No κ, supplier or selected-result change.**

**Theorem A: integer shifts need four queries at 82 odd-S arities.** In [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653)'s integer-shift alphabet, the only source change is `a += k*b` with integer `k`, and the only query is `y += q*a^3` with dyadic `q`. Let `S = r(r-1)/2` be odd.

- A mod-8 lemma, in the shifted coordinates `w = 6c-(2r-1)` that [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653) suggested, shows that exactly one node has the other parity.
- That node's weight is a nonzero integer, which forces the smaller gap below `2S`.
- The node equation factors as `(w_0+3x)(w_0+x+4y) = 3x^2-M`.

So for odd S the question is a finite computation. Over the 99 odd-S arities `3 <= r <= 200`:

- exactly 17 admit three queries, with 34 node sets in total, and every one is already covered by [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653)'s classes or certificates;
- the other 82, including **15, 22, 30, 31**, need exactly four, and a four-query certificate is given for each.

**Theorem B: twenty new three-query arities.** At 48, 49, 57, 60, 69, 84, 88, 96, 105, 112, 120, 121, 124, 132, 133, 148, 169, 177, 184 and 192, the package gives exact dyadic certificates in the [PR6212](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6212)/[PR7475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7475) general-frame contract. Each comes with a literal integer-shear program that restores both arbitrary sources. With [PR6212](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6212)'s lower bound, three queries is the exact minimum at all twenty. At five of these arities (84, 105, 121, 132, 148), two of the three rows are non-monic.

**Remaining obligations.**
- Theorem A is about the integer-shift alphabet only. 44 of the 82 arities already have three-query repairs that read `b`.
- 38 odd-S arities and the even-S arities 40, 61, 141, 165, 168, 193 and 196 remain open in general frames.
- Shear counts are upper bounds.
- Physical prices are unknown.

## Task and overlap

- **Base:** `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, which is current main.
- **Task card:** `joint-query-controller`, scope **changed**. This is the same coefficient/restoration side family as [#7475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7475), [#7478](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7478) and [#7479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7479). TASK.json gives the reason and the connection to the bottleneck.
- **What it answers:** it continues [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653)'s Open next question 1 and takes up [PR7479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7479)'s Open next question 2 (restricted families).
- **Relation to [#7539](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7539) (same team).** @mithrax-exo's [#7539](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7539) states the same two results: the same 17/82 split at odd S and the same twenty general-frame rows. This PR is meant to replace it. What it adds:
  - explicit checks that still run under `python -O`;
  - a separately written second checker that takes the other divisor route;
  - pinned predecessor sources and the registered replay;
  - a four-query certificate at each of the 82 arities, so four is exact rather than only a lower bound;
  - executed programs that restore both sources.

  My review on [#7539](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7539) lists the differences in detail. If both PRs are kept, review only one of them.
- **Overlap checks:**
  - I fetched all open PR heads from [#7480](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7480) to [#7538](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7538), plus the ledger's cubic PRs ([#6200](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6200)–[#6797](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6797)), [#7475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7475), [#7478](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7478) and [#7479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7479).
  - The nearest concurrent work is Nick Petalas (@petalas)'s [#7506](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7506). It shows that at `r = 15` any frame needs two rows of height above 64. Theorem A is complementary: it covers integer shifts of every height, at 82 arities.
  - `find_overlap.py --offline` found only the local cubic packages already cited.
  - These checks are leads, not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

CPython 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cubic-odd-s-shift-floor
```

The registered replay has five commands: `verify.py` and `independent_check.py`, each run normally and under `-O`, plus `build.py --check`. All five pass. The expected markers are `PASS_CUBIC_ODD_S_SHIFT_FLOOR` and `PASS_CUBIC_ODD_S_SHIFT_FLOOR_INDEPENDENT`.

**`verify.py`**
- Authenticates four pinned predecessor files, checks four textual anchors and [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653)'s uncovered-arity list, and rejects two byte mutations.
- Runs the complete search for Theorem A. It factors `3x^2-M` over every odd gap `|x| < 2S` with a quadratic sieve and enumerates the divisor route.
- Checks every certificate by exact coefficient comparison and recomputes the weights by elimination.
- Executes every program symbolically over all `r` retained children, and on dirty rational inputs.
- Runs nine rejection controls. Among them, the same search at `r = 12` misses [PR6653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6653)'s same-parity certificate, which shows that the parity lemma is load-bearing.

**`independent_check.py`**
- Imports neither of the other scripts.
- Takes the other route of the proof: it enumerates the larger gap over the divisors of `S·N`, uses Cipolla square roots and solves the node quadratic.
- Checks identities at six non-proportional points and runs programs in a separate interpreter.
- Rejects five mutations.

**`build.py --check`** regenerates `CERTIFICATES.json` byte for byte.

**Publication preflight.** `scripts/check_research_commit.py --check-modes --check-source-history` passes on a full-history clone (13 files, source pin `e545235`).

**What is proof and what is search.** Theorem A's search is the proof: Lemmas 3–5 make it complete, and both checkers run it in full. The twenty general-frame rows came from an external search that is not included; they are the same rows as in [#7539](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7539). They are accepted only by the exact checks. The two checkers are separate AI-assisted implementations; neither human nor proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

These are recorded in the package README and TASK.json.

1. **General frames at the 38 open odd-S arities, starting with r = 15.**
   - *First step:* extend the parity lemma to rows with even `u`, which correspond to dyadic shifts, and combine it with [#7506](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7506).
   - *Blocker:* with non-monic rows there is no integral weight, so the size bound is lost.
2. **The even-S arities 40, 61, 141, 165, 168, 193 and 196.**
   - *Local evidence (not packaged):* a search with two integer nodes `|c| <= 12000` and the third node forced found nothing.
   - *First step:* search with two non-monic rows.
3. **Prices.** Price the four-shear programs at 124, 169, 177 and 184 against `r` eager shears, using [#7475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7475)'s event inequality.
